analysis: PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Five positions are at the upper bound of the 3-5 concentrated target. Portfolio heat is a modest 1.58% but the Sortino of -10.57 signals the downside volatility is outsized relative to returns — capital preservation deserves priority. THESIS REVIEW — AMP (-10.04%): AMP is the most urgent concern. It has dropped meaningfully through what should have been a stop zone and, critically, it no longer appears on the screened candidate list, meaning it has failed the quality or trend filters this cycle. A position failing its trend screen while sitting at a 10% paper loss is a classic thesis-break signal. I strongly recommend a manual exit review on AMP outside this cycle's trade output. Freeing ~$9,352 from AMP would also create meaningful capacity for a better-quality replacement. ADBE (+0.35%): Essentially flat; the forward P/E of 9.59 and PEG of 0.64 remain compelling, but the SMA50 slope is slightly negative and earnings are 44 days out — hold but monitor. NVDA (-3.01%): On the screened list, still exceptional fundamentals; the -5.1% dip vs SMA50 is noise given the cycle. FOXA (+3.05%) and ULTA (+4.13%) are both healthy. MARKET REGIME: SPY is mixed — slightly below SMA50 but with a positive 20-day slope. Not a risk-on tape but not a confirmed downtrend either. Cash is 20%, which is appropriate. NEW BUY — TXN: Texas Instruments stands out as the one genuinely asymmetric setup this cycle. It passes every quality screen (ROE 39.7%, op margin 47.5%, PEG 0.94, EPS revision +14.4% over 60 days) and sits at 74% of its 52-week range — well clear of the extended-entry danger zone. The uptrend is confirmed and the SMA50 is rising. With only $15,477 headroom we can size a starter position at ~54 shares that risks under 1% of equity. If AMP is exited first, this position can be sized to the full 1.5% risk target (~85 shares). Cash remains a position — we propose exactly one trade, not more.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $284.00-$285.00. Prefer a minor intraday pullback to current price or the rising SMA20 rather than chasing. If price gaps above $290 before fill, skip the entry.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Texas Instruments is a dominant analog/embedded-processing franchise with structural pricing power. Op margin of 47.5%, ROE 39.7%, and a PEG of 0.94 make it one of the cheapest high-quality tech names in the S&P 500 on a growth-adjusted basis. Revenue growth of 27.7% and a +14.4% EPS upward revision in 60 days confirm the cycle is turning. FCF of $4.8B supports the dividend and buyback program. TECHNICAL: Price is in a confirmed uptrend at 74% of the 52-week range — not extended. It is +4.5% above SMA50 with the SMA50 slope still rising (+0.6%). This is a Stage 2 continuation, not a late-cycle chase. The 52-week low of $150.79 vs current ~$285 shows the stock has already made a large move and is consolidating, not topping. Entry sizing of ~54 shares within the $15,477 headroom risks ~0.91% of equity — below target but prudent given the 5-position count. Full 1.5% risk sizing (~85 shares) becomes available if AMP is exited.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) stop at $268.26 is hit on a closing basis; (2) price breaks back below SMA50 on heavy volume after entry; (3) EPS revision trend reverses materially (>5% downward cut); (4) thesis change — analog capex cycle reversal or management guidance cut. Target $330 over 3-6 months. If target is approached and thesis remains intact, consider holding for LTCG treatment past the one-year mark. Review position sizing after AMP decision.
